b:
She, the angel of the sky,
I waited
for her to seek out my doorway
and leave her footprints there

Once the month of Chithirai is born
she wanders about, all adorned,
the darling child
of our people

At the sight of the rising sun
she is filled with joy;
there is nothing
to compare with her delight

Before her voice
even the flute is defeated;
even blazing fire
looks with longing at her red eyes

I am
another servant of Bharathi,
longing to leave this ghostly form,
take on her form,
sing sweet music
and live in sweetness
note: The angel is the koel (the Indian cuckoo), a red-eyed bird whose song fills the Tamil month of Chithirai (April–May). The closing lines echo Subramania Bharathi's "Kuyil Paattu" (The Song of the Koel), and "servant of Bharathi" plays on the name of the poet Bharathidasan, which means exactly that.
